newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government and farmers have taken up battle positions as farmers begin their second - and decisive - round of protests today. The government has made its intentions clear: the farmers will not be permitted to block national roads as they did for 25 days in December and the government will not stand by if they do.

--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos clashed at yesterday's meeting of the executive of ruling party PASOK, although both presented a united front to journalists later.

--Unrest on the teachers' front: primary school teachers have called a three-day strike for early February as Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis met late into the night with secondary school teachers to resolve their demands and continuing week-long strike.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis stepped in to soothe ruffled feathers between Development Minister Vasso Papandreou and Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis yesterday.

--The time of the tractor has arrived: rallies today will serve as a dress rehearsal for the second round of farmers' protests. Justice Minister Evangelos Yannopoulos has given the police to green light to intervene.
--One of the kidnappers of a six-year-old girl is now in critical condition in hospital following a suicide attempt. Police have so far arrested six people involved in the abduction.

--Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic is reported to be considering buying a yacht in Greece, as reports come to light that the embattled leader is channelling personal funds abroad and primarily to offshore companies.
--Education and former defence minister Gerasimos Arsenis crossed swords with Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos over the government's handling of national issues.
--There have been charges levelled at the Onassion Cardiology Centre that faulty electrical equipment caused the death of at least one person.
--A leading Albanian businessmen has turned his investment attention to Greece.
--The winds that flattened a school in an outer Athens suburb threaten to do the same to Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis, battling striking teachers in primary and secondary schools.
